payload.text: Vocabulary: bound-invocation-supervisor (Rust providers::external_process::bound_invocation_supervisor::BoundInvocationSupervisor) vs detached-run-supervisor (Node cli-spawn-supervisor.mjs) -- two process-supervision roles distinguished by the lifecycle/detachment axis, not a content label ('agent' vs 'RPC').
payload.rationale: supervisor.rs (Rust) and cli-spawn-supervisor.mjs (Node) look like duplicate 'supervisor' implementations (both: bounded capture, deadlines, crash mapping, cancellation grace) but answer different questions. bound-invocation-supervisor runs a short RPC-shaped call bound to ONE invocation's own lifetime, never detached -- confirmed via source: no detach/setsid/process-group logic in supervisor.rs, 2-5s default deadlines. detached-run-supervisor runs a long agent/executor job deliberately DETACHED so it survives the crash of whatever dispatched it -- confirmed via source: cli-spawn-supervisor.mjs's detached spawn, PGID-based kill, immutable receipt publication. Naming by lifecycle (detached+crash-surviving vs bound+caller-lifetime) keeps the names correct if either mechanism's real use case shifts later. Zero live conflict today: the Rust mechanism has zero current consumers (2 native routes -- gate-bypass, version -- neither uses it); dispatch stays 100% legacy-cli. Source: dispatch-engine-liveness-hardening plan.md Phase 8 C4 investigation (invocation_service.rs, operation_provider_router.rs, providers/external_process/*, apps/fgos/src/legacy_exec.rs, docs/platform/host-invocation-routing/architecture/invocation-kernel.md).
